answer: Every epoch each head may offer one piece of work it built but did not file; those offers are published as the crowd's non-claims, and each settles once, to a head unrelated to the builder. A claim is paid only if it finishes such an offer. An opal cut from a shared timber is the offer, and the vertex where an offered piece meets its finisher is where it settles. A farm's tenth head cannot offer to its siblings and cannot use their offers, so it waits on a stranger: the supply is set by how many honest heads offer, not by how many want an answer.
